# Agent K C++ project language service

A C++ workspace is a folder containing CMakeLists.txt. Pass its folder name, not a path. Call agent_k_cpp_language_server with status at the start of a C++ language-service workflow. References, definitions, declarations, type declarations, implementations, hover, symbol search, diagnostics, document symbols, call hierarchy, and type hierarchy require that named workspace to be loaded with clangd in either indexing or ready state.

A newly loaded workspace may temporarily report indexing. The Skill can already issue semantic actions, but every result reports status, indexReady, and partial. When partial is true, explicitly say that indexing is incomplete, treat results as provisional, never interpret an empty result as not found, and never claim the result set is complete. Repeat the query after status reports ready when completeness matters. Do not unload or reload the workspace merely to wait for indexing.

For semantic C++ questions in a loaded and usable workspace, use the Language Skill before grep, rg, findstr, compiler-output scraping, or custom Clang shell commands. Shell is for builds, tests, execution, Git, and explicitly textual or regex searches. If clangd returns no result, report that first and identify any later text search as supplementary rather than equivalent semantic evidence.

Keep useful C++ workspaces loaded. Do not unload and reload between queries, load preemptively for unrelated questions, or repeat a lifecycle action when status already reports the desired state. Use load and unload only for an intentional workspace lifecycle change. Use normal Pi file tools for edits and Agent K's project terminal for builds.
